findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
findings.body: The new GET endpoint changes the logged-in user's topic notification level using only the topic ID and session cookie. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF verification, and unsubscribe explicitly skips the XHR check, so an external page can direct a logged-in user to this URL and unsubscribe or mute a topic without their consent. Render a confirmation page on GET and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST, or require an appropriately scoped unsubscribe token.

findings.title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and records notifications_changed_at. For users whose reason is still null, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once their reading time exceeds the auto-track threshold. Consequently, reading the topic after unsubscribing can silently undo the preference. Use the normal notification-change API so the unsubscribe is recorded as an explicit user choice.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally reads tu.notification_level. A logged-in user opening a forwarded unsubscribe link, or opening the link while signed into a different account that has never visited the topic, can see the topic without having a TopicUser row and receives a server error instead of an unsubscribe page. Create or initialize the user-topic preference when absent, as TopicUser.change does.
